Observational analyses report that interruptions in bridge-agent cooperation correlate with measurable declines in peripheral participation that persist for multiple subsequent rounds. Field practitioners note that bridge agents who sustain cooperation through low-participation periods are reliably associated with faster recovery, while those who defect during such windows see prolonged stagnation across connected clusters.
